introduction: “All humankind are as children in a school, and the Dawning-Points of Light … are the teachers.” The eighty passages gathered here say why the Prophets come: to educate. Left to itself, human nature is a jungle; under a gardener it becomes a garden, and what was hidden in each soul like a gem in a mine is brought out. Philosophers train minds; only the Manifestations, these readings hold, have changed the conduct of whole peoples. The guide is given whole. Beside it stand eighty voices from elsewhere, many of them teachers themselves: Socrates the midwife, Confucius, Paul on the law as schoolmaster, Hosea’s God teaching a child to walk, Locke, Milton, Wordsworth. About one in four questions the picture and ends in a question. The Buddha and the Dhammapada leave the effort with the pupil, Kant calls maturity the end of tutelage, Mencius trusts human nature and distrusts those who love to teach, and Caliban learned language only to curse.
questions: Humanity is pictured as children in need of a teacher. Kant defined enlightenment as leaving tutelage, and the Buddha told his disciples to be lamps unto themselves. In what sense can an adult remain a pupil without remaining a child?

‘Abdu’l-Bahá calls the state of nature a jungle; Mencius says human nature runs to good like water downhill, and Wordsworth would learn from a wood. What is your own view of what people are before they are taught?
The proof of a Manifestation is said to be “the education and progress of the people”. What would you look for, in a community or in a person, as evidence of that education?
Philosophers, on these readings, educate bodies and minds; the Prophets change conduct. Think of Socrates, Confucius or Aristotle. What is the difference being pointed to?

Differences of capacity are called innate, and education is said to have tremendous influence. Locke began from a blank page. How do those two starting points change what a teacher does on an ordinary day?
James warns that teachers receive the greater condemnation, and Mencius that people like too much to teach. What does a parent or teacher need in order to follow “the first educators” safely?

outside.why: “Men at all times … stand in need of one to exhort them, guide them and to instruct and teach them.” Paul: how shall they hear without a preacher? and how shall they preach, except they be sent?

Bahá’u’lláh says people always need a guide. The Buddha’s last counsel to his disciples was to be lamps unto themselves and look to no external refuge. How much of the way can anyone walk for another?

The Messengers come so that each may know “the trust of God which is latent in the reality of every soul”. Gray, in a country churchyard, on what stays latent: full many a gem the dark unfathomed caves of ocean bear.
Through these Teachings a person comes to “manifest all the potential forces with which his inmost true self hath been endowed”. Socrates called his own work midwifery: he attends souls in labour.
“All humankind are as children in a school.” Proverbs: train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old he will not depart from it.

Humanity is a school and the Manifestations its teachers. Kant defined enlightenment as leaving the schoolroom: release from self-incurred tutelage, the courage to use one’s own understanding without direction from another. Can a grown humanity still be a pupil?
An educator who was imperfect could not foster perfection; “if He were ignorant, how could He make others” wise? Jesus: if the blind lead the blind, both shall fall into the ditch.
The teacher must himself be what he teaches. Chaucer’s parson knew the proverb: if gold rust, what shall iron do?

The universal Educator must be material, human and spiritual teacher at once, with a power above nature. Plato looked for something nearer: philosophers who are kings. Why has neither philosophy nor power been enough?
The purpose is that “those who are barbed of claw should turn gentle and forbearing”. Isaiah’s picture of it: the wolf shall dwell with the lamb, and a little child shall lead them.
Savagery forsaken. Tennyson: move upward, working out the beast, and let the ape and tiger die.

Education is to turn the brutal gentle. Caliban, taught by Prospero: you taught me language; and my profit on’t is, I know how to curse. What does an education need besides instruction if it is to change a nature?
The Manifestations “endure every calamity and sore affliction, and lay down Their lives as a ransom” so that souls may live to the full. Isaiah: a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief.
Man needs a teacher “that his lamp may be lighted”. Jesus to those he taught: ye are the light of the world.
The Prophets are commanded “to water the trees of human existence”. The first Psalm: like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season.
Rightly trained, a person becomes “the gem of gems”; deprived, “the epitome of animal vices”. Pope’s man stands between: in doubt to deem himself a god, or beast.
Everything turns on education. Locke: of all the men we meet with, nine parts of ten are what they are, good or evil, by their education.

Without the true Educator man becomes “the source of all that is” dark. Mencius held that human nature tends to good of itself, as water runs downhill. Is the teacher planting something, or clearing what blocks it?
Prophets and philosophers alike have thought education the greatest concern, “so that the jungle may become a garden”. Milton: the end of learning is to repair the ruins of our first parents.
“The holy Manifestations are the ideal Gardeners of human souls.” Isaiah’s song of a vineyard, fenced and planted with the choicest vine, that brought forth wild grapes.

The state of nature is “a jungle of disorder”, fruitless until cultivated. Wordsworth sent his reader to the woods: one impulse from a vernal wood may teach you more of man than all the sages can. Is nature the thing to be trained, or a teacher?
“The hand of training of the True Educator hath ever been … engaged.” Jesus: I am the vine, ye are the branches; every branch that beareth fruit, he purgeth it.
“Human beings are like suckling babes; they must be nourished from the breast of knowledge.” Peter: as newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby.
Cradled at the bosom of the Compassionate Educator. Hosea’s God remembers teaching a child to walk: I taught Ephraim also to go, taking them by their arms.

Children left without a teacher “would become like wild animals”; so souls need a Master. Proverbs put it the old way: he that spareth his rod hateth his son. What kind of discipline does a divine education use?
The suckling babes must be nurtured until adolescence. Hebrews complains of pupils who still need milk when they ought to be teachers.
“People are observed to be like children — education is needed, and an educator.” Paul: the heir, as long as he is a child, is under tutors and governors until the time appointed of the father.
“They are like unto mere children.” Wordsworth turned the comparison round: the Child is father of the Man. What does the image of humanity as children leave out about children?
“Mankind is in the utmost imperfection. It is in need of education.” Paul: when I became a man, I put away childish things.
“The essential requirement and qualification of Prophethood is the training and guidance of the people.” Nicodemus to Jesus: we know that thou art a teacher come from God.

“The purpose of the prophetic mission is none other than the education and guidance of the people.” The Qur’an on Muḥammad: a messenger who teacheth you the Scripture and wisdom, and that which ye knew not.

Training the people is “the only result of Their mission”. The Dhammapada: you yourself must make an effort; the Buddhas are only preachers. How do the readings divide the work between teacher and taught?
Those sent to educate souls “are invariably endowed with an all-compelling power”. The crowd’s reaction to the Sermon on the Mount: he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.

The Manifestation has a body, a rational soul, and a heavenly reality which is “the source of … the education of the souls”. John’s sentence for the same joining: the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us.
“Verily Thou art the Guardian of the world and the Educator of the nations.” Elihu to Job: behold, God exalteth by his power: who teacheth like him?
Human realities are trained to “become clear and pure as mirrors” reflecting the Sun of Reality. Paul: beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, we are changed into the same image.
As the sun educates all that grows, “the Sun of Reality is the Educator of the Ideal principles of life”. Plato’s sun gives the things of the mind both their being known and their growth.

The principles the Manifestations laid down “are the causes and factors of the advancement of nations”. Carlyle thought all history the biography of great men. Is that what is being claimed here, or something different?
“The sure proof that they are the Manifestations of God is in the education and progress of the people.” Jesus: by their fruits ye shall know them.
Philosophers “have educated the world of bodies”; the Manifestations have trained souls. Paul: the world by wisdom knew not God.
Two kinds of education, material and divine. Tennyson on having only the first: knowledge comes, but wisdom lingers.

The philosophers are called material teachers. Aristotle would have refused the description: his whole ethics is about becoming good, and he scolds those who take refuge in theory. What can the prophet do that the moral philosopher cannot?
The Prophets appear “to develop immature souls into maturity”. Paul: till we all come unto a perfect man, unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ.
The third education is of the spirit, through which man is lifted “into the world of moralities”. Paul’s list of what it yields: love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness.
Muḥammad gathered warring tribes “under the pavilion of unity”. The Qur’an to those tribes: ye were enemies and He made friendship between your hearts.
Neighbouring peoples praised a man by saying “Surely he must be an Israelite!” Moses had promised it: surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.
Moses “taught the divine verses, educated the Israelite people”. His own instruction on how it was to be done: thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children.
“Whenever this world becomes dark … God will send one of His Holy Messengers.” Isaiah: thine eyes shall see thy teachers, and thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way.
“In his own generation Christ was the Supreme Master.” The officers sent to arrest him came back empty-handed: never man spake like this man.

“By the Father we mean the Educator.” Jesus forbade his disciples the titles of teacher and father: one is your Master, even Christ; and all ye are brethren. What does that do to every lesser teacher’s authority?
He taught by speech, by the pen, and sometimes “through the glance of Our eye”. Luke records one such glance: the Lord turned, and looked upon Peter.
“They have sustained all their trials so that they may guide and educate people.” Muḥammad, asked who is tried most severely: the prophets.
He bore ordeals “in order that waiting souls might become manifest”. Socrates on why he would not stop teaching Athens, whatever it cost him: I am that gadfly which God has given the state.
“The light which these souls radiate is responsible for the progress of the world.” Daniel: they that turn many to righteousness shall shine as the stars for ever and ever.
Philosophers produced a fellowship “outward and temporary”; the Manifestations changed the conduct of man. Tertullian drew the line more sharply: what has Athens to do with Jerusalem?

The philosophers could not establish universal education. Confucius, who shaped the schooling of a civilization for two thousand years, called himself a transmitter and not a maker. Where would the readings place a teacher like him?
“The powers of philosophy and politics are unable to unite various nations.” Machiavelli thought only armed prophets succeed. What kind of power, on these readings, did the unarmed ones have?
“Where there is no gardener disorder prevails.” Hobbes thought both sayings true of the uncultivated and the cultivated: man to man is an arrant wolf, and man to man is a kind of God.
“One day’s education under the inspiration of the Holy Spirit” outweighs years of the other kind. The Psalm: a day in thy courts is better than a thousand.
“Education is the cause of life.” Proverbs: take fast hold of instruction; let her not go: keep her; for she is thy life.
Education is the cause of salvation. Hosea states the converse: my people are destroyed for lack of knowledge.

Slow moral training is one way; under the love of God “there will come over him a radical change”. Aristotle knew only the slow way: we become just by doing just acts. Does sudden change last without the habits?
A person taught through the love of God is changed at once. John Wesley dated his own change to a quarter before nine one evening: I felt my heart strangely warmed.
“In the school of truth learn lessons from the teacher of love.” Confucius asked something of the pupil first: I do not open up the truth to one who is not eager to get knowledge.
He is “the Comforter and the Consoler, the true Educator”. Jesus’ promise of another Comforter who would teach all things.
“The prophets are sent to refresh the dead body of the world.” Ezekiel prophesies to dry bones, and breath comes into them.
Man is taught so as, “in his turn, to be the source of guidance to others”. Paul to Timothy: the same commit thou to faithful men, who shall be able to teach others also.
“Whoever engages in the education of children following Their teachings has followed the Prophets.” Jesus rebuked the disciples who kept children from him.
To teach children is to follow the Prophets. James warns: be not many masters, knowing that we shall receive the greater condemnation. What makes teaching the young so serious a charge?
Teachers of children walk in the Prophets’ way. Mencius: the evil of men is that they like to be teachers of others. How does a teacher keep that warning in mind?
A mother is to nurse her children “at the breast of the love of God”. Paul remembers where Timothy’s faith began: in thy grandmother Lois, and thy mother Eunice.
“Day by day may you progress”, each a sapling in the divine garden. Luke on a boy in Nazareth: Jesus increased in wisdom and stature.
The Kingdom “is in truth a divine school”. Isaiah: all thy children shall be taught of the Lord; and great shall be the peace of thy children.
A divine school with one Educator. Jeremiah foresaw a day when no one would need to teach his neighbour, for the law would be written in every heart. Is the school meant to end?
“I am educating thee so that thou mayest become worthy.” Hebrews: whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth.
Differences among people are innate, and yet “training and education … exert a tremendous influence”. Confucius: by nature, men are nearly alike; by practice, they get to be wide apart.
The Manifestations affirm that differences of capacity are inborn. Locke supposed the mind white paper, void of all characters, furnished wholly by experience. What does each view ask of a teacher?

Man evolved, but as man from the outset; what the Educators tell us is “fundamentally true”, while science “tomorrow may be entirely changed”. Darwin’s closing sentence on endless forms evolved. How should a believer hold a scientific account that is still being revised?
The Manifestation “must use the limited medium of human language”. The rabbis had a rule for reading scripture on that account: the Torah spoke in the language of men.
He must raise people from “the limited and often erroneous background” of what they know. Mark: he spake the word unto them as they were able to hear it.

isaiah-thine-eyes-shall-see-thy-teachers.text: And though the Lord give you the bread of adversity, and the water of affliction, yet shall not thy teachers be removed into a corner any more, but thine eyes shall see thy teachers: And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it, when ye turn to the right hand, and when ye turn to the left

isaiah-taught-of-the-lord.text: And all thy children shall be taught of the Lord; and great shall be the peace of thy children

hosea-taught-ephraim-to-go.text: I taught Ephraim also to go, taking them by their arms; but they knew not that I healed them. I drew them with cords of a man, with bands of love: and I was to them as they that take off the yoke on their jaws, and I laid meat unto them

job-who-teacheth-like-him.text: Behold, God exalteth by his power: who teacheth like him

john-teacher-come-from-god.text: There was a man of the Pharisees, named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews: The same came to Jesus by night, and said unto him, Rabbi, we know that thou art a teacher come from God: for no man can do these miracles that thou doest, except God be with him

galatians-under-tutors.text: Now I say, That the heir, as long as he is a child, differeth nothing from a servant, though he be lord of all; But is under tutors and governors until the time appointed of the father

ephesians-unto-a-perfect-man.text: And he gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers; For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ: Till we all come in the unity of the faith, and of the knowledge of the Son of God, unto a perfect man, unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ

deuteronomy-wise-and-understanding-peopl.text: Keep therefore and do them; for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations, which shall hear all these statutes, and say, Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people

proverbs-she-is-thy-life.text: Take fast hold of instruction; let her not go: keep her; for she is thy life

james-be-not-many-masters.text: My brethren, be not many masters, knowing that we shall receive the greater condemnation

proverbs-spareth-his-rod.text: He that spareth his rod hateth his son: but he that loveth him chasteneth him betimes

quran-teacheth-you-that-which-ye-knew-no.text: Even as We have sent unto you a messenger from among you, who reciteth unto you Our revelations and causeth you to grow, and teacheth you the Scripture and wisdom, and teacheth you that which ye knew not.

quran-taught-him-utterance.text: Hath made known the Qur'an. He hath created man. He hath taught him utterance

dhammapada-make-an-effort.text: You yourself must make an effort. The Tathagatas (Buddhas) are only preachers. The thoughtful who enter the way are freed from the bondage of Mara

dhammapada-wise-people-fashion-themselve.text: Well-makers lead the water (wherever they like); fletchers bend the arrow; carpenters bend a log of wood; wise people fashion themselves

avot-make-for-yourself-a-teacher.text: Joshua ben Perahiah used to say: appoint for thyself a teacher, and acquire for thyself a companion and judge all men with the scale weighted in his favor

shakespeare-you-taught-me-language.text: You taught me language; and my profit on't / Is, I know how to curse. The red plague rid you / For learning me your language
shakespeare-you-taught-me-language.author: William Shakespeare

source.label: The Complete Works of William Shakespeare (MIT)

locke-white-paper.text: Let us then suppose the mind to be, as we say, white paper, void of all characters, without any ideas; how comes it to be furnished? Whence comes it by that vast store which the busy and boundless fancy of man has painted on it, with an almost endless variety? Whence has it all the materials of reason and knowledge? To this I answer in one word, from experience
locke-white-paper.author: John Locke

locke-nine-parts-of-ten.text: I think I may say, that of all the men we meet with, nine parts of ten are what they are, good or evil, useful or not, by their education
locke-nine-parts-of-ten.author: John Locke

wordsworth-child-is-father.text: The Child is Father of the Man; / And I could wish my days to be / Bound each to each by natural piety
wordsworth-child-is-father.author: William Wordsworth
wordsworth-child-is-father.work: “My heart leaps up when I behold”

milton-repair-the-ruins.text: The end then of learning is to repair the ruins of our first parents by regaining to know God aright, and out of that knowledge to love him, to imitate him, to be like him
milton-repair-the-ruins.author: John Milton

dewey-process-of-living.text: I believe that education, therefore, is a process of living and not a preparation for future living
dewey-process-of-living.author: John Dewey

plato-until-philosophers-are-kings.text: Until philosophers are kings, or the kings and princes of this world have the spirit and power of philosophy, and political greatness and wisdom meet in one, and those commoner natures who pursue either to the exclusion of the other are compelled to stand aside, cities will never have rest from their evils
plato-until-philosophers-are-kings.author: Plato

plato-art-of-midwifery.text: Well, my art of midwifery is in most respects like theirs; but differs, in that I attend men and not women; and look after their souls when they are in labour, and not after their bodies
plato-art-of-midwifery.author: Plato
